group: R1 — E0-03 cancellation and A-07 emergency stop, real Claude Code and real Codex

cases.scenario: Cancel a live real Claude Code session with POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/interrupt 3 s after it is observed `active`, then close it 5 s later.
cases.agentOrSurface: real Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 driven through the interact-ai HTTP API (127.0.0.1:19010), isolated INTERACT_AI_HOME
cases.precondition: Fresh daemon (pid 91045) on port 19010 with INTERACT_AI_HOME=<out>/claude-interrupt/home and INTERACT_AI_MOBILE_ADVERTISE=0; INTERACT_AI_CLAUDE_BIN/INTERACT_AI_CODEX_BIN unset so the real CLI on PATH is used; workdir <out>/claude-interrupt/workdir containing only NOTES.md; no prior agent child processes (ps-baseline.txt empty).
steps: POST /v1/agent-sessions {agentId:claude-code, workdir, ttlMinutes:20, maxMessages:40, allowWrite:false} -> 200, state created
POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/messages {kind:task, body:{task:'1500-word Traditional-Chinese essay, no file access'}} -> 200
Poll GET /v1/agent-sessions/{id} until state==active (observed at mono 61.3 s)
Wait 3 s, POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/interrupt -> 200
Poll to terminal state; snapshot descendants of pid 91045; read from-session mailbox
Wait 5 s, POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/close {reason} -> 200; snapshot processes again
Read ~/.claude/projects/<workdir-slug>/5fd573dd-....jsonl read-only for the provider-side view

expected.ui: SSE agent.session.state and the API record both move to a cancellation state and stay consistent with each other
expected.coreState: session record state = cancelled (a human-requested stop is not a failure), with a reason the operator can read
expected.effect: the `claude -p` subprocess tree is gone, no late from-session result arrives after the cancel

cases.actual: The cancel MECHANISM works: the child was killed and nothing arrived late. The CLASSIFICATION does not. POST /interrupt returned 200 at 09:05:00.474; 0.5 s later the record read `failed` (not cancelled), with no `detail` and an empty from-session mailbox. Claude's own log shows it had streamed 287 chars of the essay before the SIGINT and then recorded '[Request interrupted by user]'; that partial output never reached the mailbox. After the later close the record still read `failed` while the SSE event emitted at the same instant said `closed`.

observations: Time from task-sent to `active` was 61.3 s for Claude (vs 1.7 s for Codex on the same box at the same moment); during that whole minute GET returned "created" while SSE had already said "fetched".
The interrupt landed within ~90 ms of Claude emitting its first text chunk, so this run is also evidence that partial output produced before an interrupt is discarded by the mailbox.
Two independent runs (claude-interrupt, b07-claude) and one diagnostic re-run (diag-failreason) all produced `failed`.

cases.scenario: Is POST /interrupt 'stop this turn' or 'end this session'? Interrupt a live Claude session, then try to send a NEW short task on the SAME session.
cases.agentOrSurface: real Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 via HTTP API 127.0.0.1:19014, isolated home; custom probe <out>/bin/b07.py
cases.precondition: Fresh daemon (pid 21899) on port 19014, isolated home, mobile advertise off, agent-bin overrides unset. Child-process checks in this probe walk only descendants of pid 21899, so other agents' processes cannot contaminate them.
steps: Create session, send the long essay task
Poll until active (65.3 s); record descendants of 21899
Wait 3 s, POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/interrupt -> 200 {"interrupted":true}
Poll to terminal; record descendants at +0 s and +2 s; read from-session
POST /v1/agent-sessions/{id}/messages {kind:task, body:{task:'只回覆一個字：好'}} and record the HTTP status
GET the record again and re-check descendants

expected.ui: if interrupt means 'stop generating', the session should return to a usable state and accept a new task
expected.coreState: session either stays open (turn-level stop) or goes terminal (session-level cancel) — the test decides which
expected.effect: a follow-up task either runs or is refused

cases.actual: POST /interrupt is a SESSION-level cancel, not a 'stop generating'. Interrupt -> state `failed` in 0.5 s; the descendant list of daemon 21899 went from ['22342 21899 claude -p ...'] to [] immediately and stayed [] at +2 s. The follow-up task was refused with HTTP 409 {"error":{"code":"conflict","message":"conflict: agent session asession-65b89fa8-... is Failed; mailbox closed"}}. There is no API path to stop the current turn and keep the session usable; the subprocess is gone, so nothing could resume in place either.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-user-Workspace-claude-lab-adaptive-interaction/95db6375-b13e-4494-9180-4b15da263657/scratchpad/e2e2/runs/R1/b07-claude/result.json task2Status=409, task2Resp.error.message="conflict: agent session asession-65b89fa8-a9a1-4234-a4aa-49b732052665 is Failed; mailbox closed"
observations: The 409 message leaks the internal Debug spelling `Failed` (capitalised) rather than the wire value `failed` that every other surface uses.
This run independently reproduces D1: a second real Claude interrupt, again `failed`, again with no `detail`.

Consequence for a UI: a 'stop' button wired to /interrupt cannot be offered as 'stop generating' — it destroys the session and the operator must create a new one (paying the ~65 s Claude cold start again).

cases.actual: Identical conclusion, different terminal label. cases.scenario: Press Emergency Stop while a real Claude session is actively generating; verify the session, its subprocess, the status projection, and the refusal of new sessions.
cases.agentOrSurface: real Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 via HTTP API 127.0.0.1:19016, isolated home; custom probe <out>/bin/a07.py
cases.precondition: Fresh daemon d1 (pid 41215) on port 19016, isolated home, mobile advertise off, agent-bin overrides unset; GET /v1/status.emergencyStop == false before the test; descendant checks scoped to pid 41215.
steps: GET /v1/status -> emergencyStop false
Create Claude session, send the long essay task, poll until active (63.2 s); record descendants of 41215
Wait 3 s, POST /v1/emergency-stop {} with the HUMAN token
GET the session record; GET /v1/status; record descendants at +0.5 s and +3 s; read from-session
POST /v1/agent-sessions again (human token) and record the status
POST /v1/emergency-stop/clear with the RESTRICTED AGENT token from <home>/state/api-agent-token and record the status

expected.ui: SSE emits emergency.stop and the session projection goes to a stopped state; /v1/status.emergencyStop true
expected.coreState: the open agent session is cancelled; consents revoked; estop latched in the store
expected.effect: the `claude -p` subprocess tree is terminated; new agent sessions are refused; the AI cannot clear the stop

cases.actual: All four invariants held. POST /v1/emergency-stop returned 200 with an itemised, honest report (stoppedActuators 14/14, unconfirmedActuators [], sensors.stopped true, sensors.uncertain false). The live session went to `cancelled` with detail "cancelled (was Active)"; SSE emitted session.stopped reason=cancelled, agent.session.state=cancelled and emergency.stop. The Claude child (pid 41483, ppid 41215) that was alive at 09:12:53 was gone 1 s after the stop and still gone at +3 s. /v1/status.emergencyStop became true. A new POST /v1/agent-sessions was refused 403 policy_blocked "emergency stop engaged; no new agent sessions". The restricted agent token was refused 403 token_scope_forbidden on /v1/emergency-stop/clear while still being able to READ emergencyStop=true.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-user-Workspace-claude-lab-adaptive-interaction/95db6375-b13e-4494-9180-4b15da263657/scratchpad/e2e2/runs/R1/a07-claude/result.json fromSessionAfterEstop[0].kind="emergency-stop" body.deliveredToAgent=false, body.reason='緊急停止：這個工作已被取消，並已對它的子程序樹送出終止（先禮貌終止，寬限後強制）；不會自動恢復。'
crates/interaction-api/src/lib.rs:505-514 vs 660-690 — /v1/emergency-stop is agent-allowed, /v1/emergency-stop/clear is not
observations: The from-session mailbox message is explicitly honest about the honesty ladder: it says a termination was SENT to the subprocess tree and that deliveredToAgent=false — it does not claim the agent acknowledged anything.
Emergency stop is the ONE cancel path that puts a truthful reason on the session (detail 'cancelled (was Active)') and a message in the mailbox; /interrupt (D3) puts neither.
The estop report distinguishes stopped from unconfirmed actuators; with 14/14 confirmed and no devices attached this run cannot exercise the degraded wording.
The agent token could still READ emergencyStop=true, which is the right asymmetry (an AI may observe the stop, not lift it).
cases.limitations: No physical actuators or paired phones were attached, so `unconfirmedActuators` / `sensors.uncertain` / `characterEmergency` were all empty — the degraded-honesty branches of emergency_stop (runtime.rs:1190-1215) are NOT covered by this run. The subprocess death is from ps snapshots at +1 s/+3 s. actualModel is unknown here because the kill preceded the provider log flush.
cases.cleanup: Covered by A-07-estop-restart: daemon d1 SIGTERMed, d2 SIGTERMed after the clear; both verified dead, no listener on 19016.

cases.scenario: After the emergency stop, SIGTERM the daemon and restart it against the same INTERACT_AI_HOME: the stop must not auto-recover, and only a human may clear it.
cases.agentOrSurface: interact-ai daemon restart on 127.0.0.1:19016 (same isolated home), continuation of the A-07 Claude run
cases.precondition: Emergency stop engaged by A-07-estop-claude; daemon d1 pid 41215 running; the cancelled Claude session asession-0be8d3e6-580c-415c-829f-94de61acea85 persisted in that home.
steps: SIGTERM daemon d1 (41215); wait for exit; confirm /v1/ready no longer answers
Spawn daemon d2 against the SAME home and port; wait for /v1/ready
GET /v1/status -> emergencyStop must still be true
GET the original session -> state must still be cancelled
POST /v1/agent-sessions -> must still be refused
POST /v1/emergency-stop/clear with the HUMAN token -> 200
GET /v1/status -> emergencyStop false; POST /v1/agent-sessions -> 200; close that probe session; SIGTERM d2

expected.ui: after restart the status projection still reports emergencyStop true; clearing emits emergency.stop {cleared:true}
expected.coreState: estop_engaged persisted in the store survives the restart; the cancelled session is not resurrected
expected.effect: session creation stays blocked until a human clears, then works

cases.actual: d1 exited on SIGTERM (returncode -15) and /v1/ready went false. d2 (pid 51232) came up on the same home in 0.26 s and reported emergencyStop=true — the stop did NOT auto-recover. The original session still read `cancelled` / "cancelled (was Active)" (not resurrected, not re-run). A new POST /v1/agent-sessions was still refused 403 policy_blocked. POST /v1/emergency-stop/clear with the human token returned 200 {"cleared":true}, /v1/status.emergencyStop went false, and the next POST /v1/agent-sessions succeeded (200, created) — which I then closed. Audit on the restarted daemon carries emergency.clear actor=api and character.session.emergency engaged=false.

/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-user-Workspace-claude-lab-adaptive-interaction/95db6375-b13e-4494-9180-4b15da263657/scratchpad/e2e2/runs/R1/a07-claude/result.json auditTail: kind=emergency.clear actor=api @09:13:02.258; kind=character.session.truth truth="emergency" @09:13:01.674 (re-projected on restart before the clear)
crates/interaction-runtime/src/runtime.rs:1116-1118 (store.set_meta estop_engaged true) and runtime.rs:1253-1256 (clear only via explicit human call)
observations: On restart the runtime re-projected truth="emergency" to the character layer (audit at 09:13:01.674) before any client asked — the stop is re-announced, not silently latched.
The whole restart-to-clear sequence took ~2.5 s, so a restarted daemon is blocked from the first request onward; there is no window in which a new session could slip through.
The cleared session created afterwards never received a task, so no additional provider spend.
cases.limitations: Only SIGTERM was tested here (SIGKILL restart behaviour was covered by the previous round's restart-* runs, not re-run in R1). Only the API clear path was tested; the CLI `emergency-stop --clear` and the estop-file watcher (runtime.rs:2403-2435) were not exercised.
cases.cleanup: Daemon d2 (51232) SIGTERMed by the probe; I verified with `ps -p` that 41215 and 51232 are both gone, no listener on 19016, and no orphan `claude -p` child of either.

openQuestions: D1 minimal fix: should ClaudeHandle latch an `interrupt_requested` flag (claude.rs:354) so the next error `result` maps to TaskCancelled, or should gateway.rs remember that a human interrupt was issued for this session? The second is connector-agnostic and would also cover future connectors.

D2: should close emit the record's actual state string verbatim, or should the event carry BOTH `state` and a separate `closed:true` field so consumers can tell 'failed and now closed' from 'closed cleanly'?
Is `error_during_execution` stable across Claude Code versions? If the fix keys on that subtype rather than on an interrupt latch it will silently rot.

D4: Codex's turn/interrupt already aborts only the turn (turn_aborted) and the runtime kills the process anyway. Is a turn-level stop wanted as a distinct API verb (e.g. POST .../stop-turn), and is it even expressible for Claude's -p mode?

The ~63 s Claude cold start (task-sent -> working) was consistent across all five Claude runs. Is that the MCP config load in `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {...}`, and does it belong in the Phase 0 baseline as a usability defect?

Should partial agent output produced before a cancel be written into the from-session mailbox (it currently survives only as an `agent.session` observation), or is discarding it the intended honesty behaviour?
notes: R1 ran 7 real-agent sessions (5 Claude Code 2.1.263, 4 Codex 0.153.4 — counting the B-07 pair and the diagnostic) on ports 19010-19017, each with its own daemon and INTERACT_AI_HOME under the R1 out directory. No repo file was modified and nothing was built. Every daemon I spawned (91045, 91044, 5662, 5661, 21899, 21898, 41215, 51232, 71157) is confirmed dead and no `claude -p` / `codex app-server` descendant of any of them survives; ~/.adaptive-interaction, ~/.claude and ~/.codex were only read. Headline results: emergency stop (A-07) passes every invariant I could exercise on this hardware — live session cancelled, subprocess killed, status latched true across a SIGTERM restart, new sessions 403, and the restricted agent token refused the clear while still able to read the flag. Cancellation (E0-03) works mechanically on both agents and in both modes, but Claude's /interrupt is misreported as `failed` with no reason attached, while Codex reports `cancelled` — same call, same runtime, two different honesty outcomes. B-07 has a clean answer: /interrupt is a session-level cancel on BOTH agents (409 'mailbox closed' on the follow-up task), so there is currently no 'stop generating' capability. Two additional defects fell out of the evidence rather than the plan: the close event projects `closed` over a record that stayed `failed` (D2), and a failed session carries no reason on the record or in the mailbox (D3) — the cause exists only as an `agent.session` observation reading `error_during_execution`. D1/D2/D3 are all small, local, Phase-0-sized fixes. Model identity is provider-local only, as required: Claude runs came back claude-fable-5-1 / permissionMode plan, Codex runs gpt-6-astra with approval_policy untrusted and sandbox read-only; two Claude runs (claude-close, a07-claude) have actualModel unknown because the kill preceded the provider log flush and I did not infer them from sibling runs.
